## Scope clarification and partial reductions

The substantive closed genus-at-least-two version of KP2.17 remains **unsolved**. This package does not classify currents having the full hyperbolic length function of an arbitrary self-intersecting closed geodesic.

It records the exact all-metric Liouville-intersection fiber, the classical reduction to measured-lamination intersection data (whose converse fails), compact convex fibers, and rigidity for a simple reference curve. Compactness and finite matrix tests are not substituted for a finite-support theorem.

There is a scoped counterexample under the complete finite-area punctured-surface convention: the thrice-punctured sphere has singleton Teichmüller space, and a scaled non-atomic Liouville current matches any chosen nonperipheral closed-geodesic length. This convention must be distinguished from a compact-core current space or a pair of pants with variable boundary lengths. The K3 book's broad chapter conventions and the problem's unstated closedness make this a source-scope issue; no campaign closed-surface solution or historical-priority credit is claimed.

The actual original question is in the K3 book, printed pp.98–99. The dataset's AIM URL points only to a four-page workshop summary. Full source pointers, the current Leininger/Jyothis equivalence distinctions and the noncompact-current caveat are included.

## Review and checks

Separate adversarial mathematical/source review passed for this explicitly partial scope, with 72 independent exact assertions. It is included before this draft opens. Run `python3 unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/2765/verify.py` (SymPy1.14.0). It passes 30 exact matrix/free-word controls, including the explicit hyperbolic Γ(2) element and a generic trace-reversal identity. These are not finite tests of the full all-Teichmüller-space current condition.

Actual model: gpt-6-astra xhigh. Two substantive attempts, then a precise stop at the closed-surface finite-support/convex-decomposition gap. The coordinator owns the QUEUE update to unsolved.
